newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: ASEAN ministers meet on site of old tin mine.
newsitem.headline: ASEAN ministers meet on site of old tin mine.

text.p: Africa surrounded Southeast Asian foreign ministers on Friday.

The 441-room Sunway Lagoon Resort Hotel where they met for the 30th anniversary of the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) was modelled on Sun City, a South African entertainment and gambling complex in the bush near Johannesburg.

As they gathered for their historic meeting, ministers representing nine countries and half a billion people a world away from Africa were embraced by a "lost city", Disney World-type theme of safaris and ancient Egypt.
Life-sized tigers chasing and leaping on a group of antelope cast in bronze dominated the entrance to the hotel.
Still under construction was what started out as a giant replica of the sphinx.
Then someone realised that human, or even semi-human, images were contrary to Islam, Malaysia's main religion, and the sphinx was hurriedly turned into a lion.
"It's certainly different," commented the wife of a senior minister.
